newsitem.title: USA: Detroit committee recommends site for new casinos.
newsitem.headline: Detroit committee recommends site for new casinos.

text.p: An advisory committee to Detroit Mayor Dennis Archer recommended Friday that casino developments be clustered within a 100 acre site in the northwest portion of the city's central business district.
The committee's recommendation steers clear of the existing Greektown entertainment area and the future site of stadiums for the Detroit Lions football team and Detroit Tigers baseball club.
Michigan voters last November approved a referendum permitting three casinos within Detroit city limits. Archer created the committee to recommend a site for the casinos and other guidelines.
Archer said Friday after receiving the report that he hopes to issue a formal license application with city requirements on June 20.
While the committee did not recommend the Greektown area, Archer said all sites discussed in the report remain in play until all factors have been considered.
Bids for casino licenses must be submitted by July 18 and each application will cost $50,000.
Archer has said he would like licenses awarded by the end of the year and construction to begin in early 1998 if possible.

The referendum approved by voters also included a "preferred parties" clause giving preference to local entities Greektown Casino LLC and the Atwater Group if they are found qualified for licensing and a limited number of applications are received.

Michigan lawmakers are considering eliminating those preferences from the law and the Lac View Desert Band of the Lake Superior Chippewa Indians has filed a federal lawsuit challenging the referendum.
The committee also recommended that no temporary casinos be established during construction of the entertainment centers and that Detroit residents comprise at least 30 percent of the workforce.

Archer said he would be willing to listen to plans for temporary casinos if developers pursue that possibility and added that it would take a "very compelling" argument for him to advocate Detroit residents comprising anything less than 50 percent of casino employees.

Referendum backers believe the casinos could generate more than $100 million annually in tax revenue and have estimated as much as $1 million of gambling business leaves Michigan for Windsor, Ontario, every day.

A number of groups have announced interest in seeking a license, including Detroit businessman Don Barden, owner and operator of the Majestic Star Casino in Gary, Ind., Circus Circus Enterprises Inc., joining with Atwater Group, MGM Grand Inc, Mirage Resorts Inc. and Harrah's Entertainment Inc.
